mainTopic: Rare words the חכמים learned from everyday speech, and the משנה and גמרא on which shape of שופר is blown on ראש השנה, the יובל, and fast days
overview: The amud opens by finishing a series of stories about rare words. לוי did not know the word קבע, and the בית מדרש showed from a פסוק in מלאכי that it means 'rob.' רבא מברניש says he would have worked it out by asking the man questions, and the גמרא explains why לוי did not. Then the חכמים learn four words from רבי's maidservant (סירוגין, חלוגלוגות, סלסלה, and the words for 'sweep' and 'broom'), and a fifth, יהב ('load'), from an Arab traveler. Next comes a new משנה. On ראש השנה a straight ibex שופר is blown with trumpets beside it, and the שופר gets the long blast. On fast days curved ram horns are used, and the trumpets get the long blast. The יובל matches ראש השנה, but רבי יהודה disagrees about which horn is used. In the גמרא, רבי לוי rules that curved horns are used on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים of the יובל. The גמרא shows he follows רבי יהודה only in part. It ends by explaining that the dispute is about whether a day calls for a bent, humble mind or a straight one.

steps.title: A strange word: someone says 'so-and-so did קבע to me'
steps.stepSummary: A man tells לוי that someone did 'קבען' to him. לוי does not understand the word and goes to ask in the בית מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'So-and-so did קבע to me.' He did not know what the man was saying to him. He went and asked in the בית מדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of לוי continues. A man uses the unknown word קבען, and לוי goes to the בית מדרש to find out what it means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is purely about vocabulary: לוי cannot rule on the man's complaint because he does not know what the key word means. Instead of guessing, he asks in the בית מדרש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He did קבע to me': the unknown word in this story

phrases.english: "So-and-so kava'a me."

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה יָדַע מַאי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He did not know what he was saying to him.
He went and asked in the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא הֲוָה יָדַע מַאי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of stories about unfamiliar words from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the word קבע mean?

steps.title: The study hall explains: קבע means 'robbed'
steps.stepSummary: The בית מדרש tells לוי that קבע means 'robbed,' and proves it from the פסוק 'Will a man rob God?'
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: He told you 'He robbed me,' as it is written: 'Will a man rob (hayikba) God?'
steps.whatsHappening: The people in the בית מדרש answer לוי's question. קבע means to rob, and they show this from a פסוק in מלאכי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They find the same root, קבע, used in a פסוק where it clearly means robbing. So the man's complaint was that someone stole from him.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: They said to him: "He robbed me" is what he told you,
as it is written: "Will a man rob God?" and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the meaning of קבע.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קבע means 'to rob,' as shown by the פסוק in מלאכי.

steps.title: רבא מברניש: I would have figured it out by asking questions
steps.stepSummary: רבא מברניש tells רב אשי that he would have asked the man 'how, with what, and why' and worked out the meaning on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא מברניש said to רב אשי: Had I been there, I would have said to him: How did he do קבע to you? With what did he do קבע to you? And why did he do קבע to you? And from that I would have understood on my own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא מברניש suggests that לוי did not need to go ask anyone. He could have asked the man a few questions and worked out the meaning from the answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works like a challenge to לוי's approach. Why leave to ask, when the man's own explanation would have shown what the word meant?

keyTerms.meaning: רבא from the place called ברניש

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִבַּרְנִישׁ לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rava from Barnish said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הֲוַאי הָתָם, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Had I been there, I would have said to him:
How did he kava you? With what did he kava you?
And why did he kava you?
And from that I would have known on my own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הֲוַאי הָתָם, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how לוי went about finding the meaning.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's decision to go ask in the בית מדרש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Asking the man about the details would have shown what the word meant, so there was no need to go elsewhere.

steps.title: לוי thought it was a matter of איסור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that לוי thought the man was asking about something forbidden, not about money, so those questions would not have helped.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he (לוי) thought the man was talking about a matter of prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends לוי. He did not realize this was a money case, so asking 'how, with what, why' would not have seemed useful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Questions like 'with what did he do it to you' fit a case about money or damage. לוי assumed the man was asking about an איסור, where those questions would not reveal the meaning of the word.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter of prohibition (איסור), as opposed to money

phrases.english: And he thought:
He is speaking to him about a matter of prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא מברניש's challenge to לוי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the mindset of the person being challenged
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוי could easily have worked out the word by asking the man questions.
steps.terutzMaskana: לוי assumed it was a question about an איסור, where those questions would not have helped.
steps.whatToRemember: קבע means 'rob' (from מלאכי). לוי asked in the בית מדרש instead of questioning the man, because he thought it was a matter of איסור and not money.

steps.title: סירוגין means 'on and off,' learned from רבי's maidservant
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים did not know the word סירוגין. They heard רבי's maidservant use it for people coming in a few at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים did not know what סירוגין means. They heard the maidservant of רבי's house, who saw the חכמים entering in small groups, say to them: How long will you come in סירוגין סירוגין?
steps.whatsHappening: A new word story begins. The maidservant in רבי's house used the word סירוגין for people entering in bits and pieces, and from that the חכמים learned that it means 'at intervals.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from everyday speech. She said סירוגין while describing something they could see, people coming in a few at a time, so the meaning became obvious.

phrases.english: The Sages did not know what "seirugin" means.
They heard the maidservant of Rabbi's house,
who saw the Sages
who were coming in a few at a time,
and she said to them:

phrases.aramaic: עַד מָתַי אַתֶּם נִכְנָסִין סֵירוּגִין סֵירוּגִין.
phrases.english: "How long will you keep coming in seirugin seirugin?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to another story about a word that was unclear.
steps.raayaObject: The meaning of the word סירוגין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The maidservant's remark to the חכמים who were entering in small groups

steps.title: חלוגלוגות means purslane
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים did not know the word חלוגלוגות. They heard the maidservant use it for a man scattering his purslane.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים did not know what חלוגלוגות means. One day they heard the maidservant of רבי's house, who saw a man scattering his purslane, say to him: How long will you scatter your חלוגלוגות?
steps.whatsHappening: Another word is solved the same way. The maidservant called the purslane a man was scattering חלוגלוגות, so they learned that חלוגלוגות is purslane.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, she used the unclear word while pointing at something real. The Aramaic word פרפחינא, which they knew, matches the Hebrew word חלוגלוגות, which they did not.

phrases.english: The Sages did not know what "haloglogot" means.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד שַׁמְעוּהָ לְאַמְּתָא דְבֵי רַבִּי
phrases.english: One day they heard the maidservant of Rabbi's house,
who saw a certain man
scattering his purslane,
and she said to him:
"How long will you keep scattering your haloglogot?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story in the same pattern: a word learned from the maidservant.
steps.raayaObject: The meaning of the word חלוגלוגות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The maidservant's remark to a man scattering purslane

steps.title: סלסלה means 'turn it about,' like curling hair
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים did not understand סלסלה in the פסוק. They heard the maidservant say it to a man curling his hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים did not know what 'סלסלה and it will exalt you' means. One day they heard the maidservant of רבי's house speaking to a man who was curling his hair. She said to him: How long will you be מסלסל your hair?
steps.whatsHappening: The third story solves a word from a פסוק in משלי. The maidservant used מסלסל for curling or twisting hair, so they learned that סלסלה means 'turn it over and over.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the word means turning something about, the פסוק reads: keep turning wisdom over, and it will raise you up. This time everyday speech explains a word in a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Turn it about, and it will exalt you

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲווֹ יָדְעִי רַבָּנַן מַאי: ״סַלְסְלֶהָ וּתְרוֹמְמֶךָּ״.
phrases.english: The Sages did not know what "salseleha and it will exalt you" means.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד שַׁמְעוּהָ לְאַמְּתָא דְבֵי רַבִּי
phrases.english: One day they heard the maidservant of Rabbi's house
speaking to a certain man
who was curling his hair.
She said to him:
"How long will you keep curling your hair?"

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא הֲווֹ יָדְעִי רַבָּנַן מַאי: ״סַלְסְלֶהָ וּתְרוֹמְמֶךָּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third story in the same maidservant pattern, this time explaining a word in a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The meaning of סלסלה in משלי 4:8
steps.raayaSupportSource: The maidservant's remark to a man curling his hair

steps.title: Learning the word for 'sweep' from the maidservant
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים did not understand וטאטאתיה במטאטא השמד until they heard רבי's maidservant tell her friend to take a broom and sweep the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים did not know what 'And I will sweep it with the broom of destruction' means. One day they heard the maidservant of רבי's house saying to her friend: 'Take a broom and sweep the house.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is another example in the list: a hard word in a פסוק became clear from how the maidservant spoke at home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words טאטאתיה and מטאטא were unclear to the חכמים. When the maidservant used טאטיתא for 'broom' and טאטי for 'sweep,' they saw that the פסוק means 'I will sweep it away with a broom of destruction.'

phrases.english: The Sages did not know
what 'And I will sweep it with the broom of destruction' means
One day they heard
the maidservant of רבי's house
who was saying to her friend
Take a broom and sweep the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth example of a word learned from רבי's maidservant.
steps.raayaObject: The meaning of וטאטאתיה and מטאטא in the פסוק
steps.raayaSupportSource: The maidservant's everyday words שקולי טאטיתא וטאטי ביתא

steps.title: Learning the word for 'load' from an Arab traveler
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים did not understand יהבך in השלך על ה׳ יהבך. רבה בר בר חנה reports that an Arab told him to take his יהב and throw it on the camel, showing that יהב means a load.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים did not know what 'Cast your load upon ה׳ and He will sustain you' means. רבה בר בר חנה said: One day I was traveling with a certain Arab, and I was carrying a load. He said to me: 'Take your load and throw it on my camel.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last example in the list. This time the meaning comes from an Arab traveler, as told by רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יהבך in the פסוק was unclear. The Arab called רבה בר בר חנה's burden יהביך, so the פסוק means 'throw your burden onto ה׳, and He will carry you.'
steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים learned hard words by listening to ordinary people speak. From רבי's maidservant they learned סירוגין ('at intervals'), חלוגלוגות (purslane), סלסלה ('turn it about'), and טאטא ('sweep' / 'broom'). From an Arab traveler they learned יהב ('load').

phrases.english: The Sages did not know

phrases.aramaic: מַאי ״הַשְׁלֵךְ עַל ה׳ יְהָבְךָ וְהוּא יְכַלְכְּלֶךָ״
phrases.english: what 'Cast your load upon ה׳ and He will sustain you' means
רבה בר בר חנה said:
One day I was traveling
with a certain Arab
I was carrying a load
and he said to me:
Take your load and throw it on my camel.
phrases.notes: He used the same word, יהב, for 'load.' That is how the פסוק became clear.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא הֲווֹ יָדְעִי רַבָּנַן מַאי ״הַשְׁלֵךְ עַל ה׳ יְהָבְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as before, but this time the source is an Arab traveler instead of the maidservant.
steps.raayaObject: The meaning of יהבך in the פסוק
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Arab's words to רבה בר בר חנה: שקול יהביך ושדי אגמלאי

steps.title: The שופר and trumpets on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: on ראש השנה the שופר is a straight ibex horn with a gold-plated mouth. Two trumpets stand at the sides. The שופר blows long and the trumpets short, because the main מצוה of the day is the שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The שופר of ראש השנה is a straight ibex horn, and its mouth is plated with gold. There are two trumpets on the sides. The שופר blows long and the trumpets blow short, because the מצוה of the day is with the שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It describes what kind of שופר was used on ראש השנה and how the trumpets were blown alongside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a שופר and trumpets are blown, but the שופר gets the more important role. It is placed in the middle and its blast lasts longer. The reason given is that the day's real מצוה is the שופר.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)

phrases.english: משנה:
The שופר of ראש השנה
is of a straight ibex horn
and its mouth is plated with gold
and two trumpets on the sides
The שופר blows long and the trumpets blow short
because the מצוה of the day is with the שופר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the end of the list of hard words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש השנה a straight, gold-mouthed ibex שופר is blown together with two trumpets beside it. The שופר's blast is longer because the day's מצוה is the שופר.

steps.title: The שופרות and trumpets on fast days
steps.stepSummary: On fast days curved ram horns with silver-plated mouths are used, with two trumpets in the middle. The שופר blows short and the trumpets long, because the main מצוה of the day is the trumpets.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on fast days they use curved rams' horns, and their mouths are plated with silver. There are two trumpets in the middle. The שופר blows short and the trumpets blow long, because the מצוה of the day is with the trumpets.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues by describing fast days, which work the opposite way from ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every detail flips. The horns are curved ram horns instead of a straight ibex horn, and they are plated with silver instead of gold. The trumpets move to the middle and get the long blast, because on a fast day the main מצוה is the trumpets.
steps.whatToRemember: Whichever instrument carries the day's מצוה gets the long blast: the שופר on ראש השנה and the trumpets on fast days.
steps.confusionAlert: On ראש השנה there is one שופר with two trumpets beside it. On fast days the משנה speaks of several horns (פיהן, 'their mouths') with the two trumpets in the middle between them.

phrases.english: And on fast days, with curved rams' horns
and their mouths are plated with silver
and two trumpets in the middle
The שופר blows short and the trumpets blow long
because the מצוה of the day is with the trumpets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets fast days against ראש השנה, reversing each detail.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On fast days curved, silver-mouthed ram horns are used with trumpets in the middle. The trumpets get the long blast because the day's מצוה is the trumpets.

steps.title: יום הכפורים of the יובל matches ראש השנה; רבי יהודה disagrees about the horn
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says יום הכפורים of the יובל year is the same as ראש השנה for the blowing and the ברכות. רבי יהודה says ראש השנה uses rams' horns while the יובל uses ibex horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Jubilee is the same as ראש השנה for the blowing and the blessings. רבי יהודה says: on ראש השנה we blow with rams' horns, and in Jubilee years with ibex horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and compares the יובל's יום הכפורים to ראש השנה. Then רבי יהודה gives his different view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion (the תנא קמא) says the two days are fully alike, so both use the straight ibex horn from step 10. רבי יהודה splits them: rams' horns for ראש השנה and ibex horns for the יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jubilee year (every 50th year); here it means its יום הכפורים, when the שופר is blown
The extra blessings added to the עמידה
Rams (male sheep), whose horns are curved
Ibexes (wild goats), whose horns are straight

phrases.english: The Jubilee is the same as Rosh HaShana
phrases.notes: He means יום הכפורים of the Jubilee year, when the שופר is blown.

phrases.english: for the blowing and for the blessings.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
On Rosh HaShana we blow with rams' horns
and in Jubilee years with ibex horns.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁוֶה הַיּוֹבֵל לְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לַתְּקִיעָה וְלַבְּרָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of שופרות for different occasions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: the יובל matches ראש השנה. רבי יהודה: rams' horns on ראש השנה, ibex horns in the יובל.

steps.title: רבי לוי: curved horns on ראש השנה and יום הכפורים, straight horns the rest of the year
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי rules that ראש השנה and יום הכפורים of the יובל use curved horns, and the rest of the year (fast days) uses straight horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: the מצוה of ראש השנה and of יום הכפורים is with curved horns, and the rest of the year is with straight horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling from רבי לוי about which shape of שופר to use on each occasion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the reverse of our משנה, which gave straight horns to ראש השנה and curved horns to fast days. That clash sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The rest of the year; here, the fast days

phrases.english: Gemara: Rabbi Levi said:
The מצוה of Rosh HaShana
and of Yom Kippur is with curved horns,
phrases.notes: This is יום הכפורים of the Jubilee year, the one the משנה just mentioned.

phrases.english: and that of the rest of the year is with straight ones.
phrases.notes: The 'rest of the year' means the fast days, the other time a שופר is blown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with an אמורא's ruling on the משנה's topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Curved horns for ראש השנה and יום הכפורים of the יובל; straight horns for fast days.

steps.title: But the משנה says the ראש השנה שופר is a straight ibex horn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי לוי from our משנה, which says the ראש השנה שופר is a straight ibex horn.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: the שופר of ראש השנה is a straight ibex horn!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי לוי's ruling by quoting the משנה from step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי לוי said curved for ראש השנה, but the משנה clearly says straight. An אמורא is not supposed to go against an unnamed משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But we learned in a משנה': introduces a challenge from a משנה

phrases.english: But we learned in the Mishnah:
The shofar of Rosh HaShana
is a straight ibex horn!
phrases.notes: This is the משנה we saw back in step 10.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי לוי's ruling that ראש השנה uses curved horns.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The unnamed משנה says the ראש השנה שופר is straight, which directly contradicts him.

steps.title: רבי לוי follows רבי יהודה's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי לוי follows רבי יהודה, who says in a ברייתא that ראש השנה uses curved rams' horns and the יובל uses ibex horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it like this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says, on ראש השנה they would blow with curved rams' horns, and in Jubilee years with ibex horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי לוי by showing he follows a different תנא, רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי לוי is not inventing a view against the משנה. He is siding with רבי יהודה, whose ברייתא says the rams' horns are curved. So he has a תנא to rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like this תנא': he follows a specific תנא's opinion

phrases.english: He said it in line with this Tanna
as a Baraisa teaches: Rabbi Yehuda says:
On Rosh HaShana they would blow
with curved rams' horns,
and in Jubilee years with ibex horns.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא דְּאָמַר כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the ruling to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי לוי seemed to contradict the משנה with no support.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי לוי follows רבי יהודה's ברייתא about curved rams' horns on ראש השנה.

steps.title: Why not just say the הלכה follows רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי לוי stated his own ruling instead of simply saying 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him just say: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the way רבי לוי worded his ruling. Why the long statement?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי לוי just agrees with רבי יהודה, a short line saying so would do. His separate wording suggests he means something more.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So let him say': asks why a simpler wording was not used

phrases.english: So let him say: the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer and questions רבי לוי's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רבי לוי's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he follows רבי יהודה, a short 'the הלכה follows him' would have been enough.

steps.title: He only agrees with רבי יהודה about ראש השנה, not the יובל
steps.stepSummary: Saying 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה' would suggest רבי לוי also agrees about ibex horns for the יובל. He does not, so he wrote his own ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you had said the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, I would have thought he agrees with רבי יהודה about the יובל too. So he teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי לוי's own wording was needed to show he agrees with רבי יהודה only in part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה uses ibex horns, which are straight, for the יובל. רבי לוי says יום הכפורים of the יובל uses curved horns. So he agrees with רבי יהודה about ראש השנה but not about the יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I would have thought': the mistaken first assumption
'He teaches us': the new point being made

steps.whatToRemember: רבי לוי follows רבי יהודה only for curved horns on ראש השנה. For the יובל he also uses curved horns, not רבי יהודה's ibex horns.

phrases.english: If you had said the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
I would have thought:
that even regarding the Jubilee too
he holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: That would mean ibex horns for the Jubilee. רבי לוי said curved horns for it in step 13.

phrases.english: so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ הִלְכְתָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording by blocking a mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A short ruling would imply he agrees with רבי יהודה about ibex horns for the יובל as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: He agrees only about ראש השנה; for the יובל he uses curved horns.

steps.title: What is the underlying disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea lies behind the disagreement about curved and straight horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move: it asks for the reason behind the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use curved and straight horns, but for opposite days. The גמרא wants the idea that drives each choice.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What are they arguing about?': asks for the root of a dispute

phrases.english: What are they arguing about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wording to the reasoning behind the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The idea behind each side's choice of curved or straight horns.

steps.title: Bending the mind in humility versus keeping it straight
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that on ראש השנה it is better to bend one's mind, so a curved horn is used, and on יום הכפורים better to keep it straight. The משנה's תנא holds the reverse: straight on ראש השנה and bent on fast days.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds: on ראש השנה, the more a person bends his mind, the better; on יום הכפורים, the more he straightens his mind, the better. The other master holds: on ראש השנה, the more he straightens his mind, the better; on fast days, the more he bends his mind, the better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the shape of the שופר matches the right state of mind for each day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A curved horn stands for a bent, humble mind, and a straight horn for a straight, plain mind. רבי יהודה wants humility on ראש השנה. The משנה's תנא wants a straight mind on ראש השנה and humility on fast days.

keyTerms.meaning: Straightens his mind: prays plainly and honestly

steps.whatToRemember: The shape of the שופר matches the mood of the day: curved means a humble, bent mind, and straight means a plain, straight mind.

phrases.english: One master holds:
phrases.notes: This first view is רבי יהודה's.

phrases.aramaic: בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה — כַּמָּה דְּכָיֵיף אִינִישׁ דַּעְתֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: On Rosh HaShana, the more a person bends his mind,
the better;

phrases.aramaic: וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים — כַּמָּה דְּפָשֵׁיט אִינִישׁ דַּעְתֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: and on Yom Kippur, the more a person straightens his mind,
the better.
And the other master holds:
phrases.notes: This is the unnamed תנא of our משנה.

phrases.aramaic: בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה — כַּמָּה דְּפָשֵׁיט אִינִישׁ דַּעְתֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: On Rosh HaShana, the more a person straightens his mind,
the better;
and on fast days, the more a person bends his mind,
the better.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כַּמָּה דְּכָיֵיף אִינִישׁ דַּעְתֵּיהּ טְפֵי מְעַלֵּי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about which days call for a bent, humble mind (curved horn) and which call for a straight mind (straight horn).
